why: four-minute technique anyone can apply immediately
posts:
If your two best teams landed in the same group, that is not bad luck.

That is what happens when you draw names out of a hat.

Snake seeding takes four minutes and removes the problem entirely. Here is how:

Step 1. Rank your teams by strength, top to bottom.

Last season's results, your own judgement, anything. Precision is not the point — having an order is.

Step 2. Split the list into pots, one pot per group.

16 teams, 4 groups → four pots of four.
Pot 1: ranks 1–4. Pot 2: ranks 5–8. And so on.

Step 3. Deal pot 1 left to right: A, B, C, D.

Step 4. Deal pot 2 right to left: D, C, B, A.

Pot 3 goes left to right again. Pot 4 right to left. That zigzag is where the name comes from.

The result: every group now holds exactly one team from each pot.

Strongest and weakest end up together. Second strongest sits with second weakest. Total group strength evens out almost perfectly.

The knockout bracket uses the same idea, simpler: seed 1 goes to the top half, seed 2 to the bottom half.

Now they cannot meet before the final. Seeds 3 and 4 split the remaining quarters.

All of this fits on one sheet of paper and takes four minutes.

It is the difference between a tournament where the final is actually the final, and one where the best match happened in round one.
